principles: Keep a cushion of easy-access savings for surprises, separate from money you plan to spend.
Size it from your essential costs, not your whole spending.
Build it in small, automatic steps on payday, with each bank's deposits kept within the protection limit.

gentle.title: A cushion for surprises
gentle.body: Your savings of {savings_balance} would cover about {emergency_fund_months} months of essentials, which run to {essential_monthly_spend} a month. A few months' cushion makes a broken boiler or a gap between jobs much less stressful. Even a small amount set aside each payday adds up, and a cash ISA lets you save up to {fact:isa_allowance} a year tax-free.

blunt.title: Your safety net is thin
blunt.body: Your savings of {savings_balance} cover {emergency_fund_months} months of essentials at {essential_monthly_spend} a month. One surprise bill could push you into debt. On payday, set aside a fixed amount in easy-access savings; a cash ISA takes up to {fact:isa_allowance} a year tax-free, and deposits up to {fact:fscs_deposit_limit} per bank are protected.
